findings.title: ReportViewSet.generate (POST /api/reports/generate/) and status/download actions have no permission_classes and rely solely on the project-wide AllowAny default, letting unauthenticated requests reach report-generation business logic

artifacts: config/settings/base.py:159-167 sets DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES=[AllowAny] project-wide and no settings module overrides it
apps/reports/api/views.py:18-25 ReportViewSet class body has no permission_classes attribute

apps/reports/api/views.py:48-75 `generate` action has no @action(permission_classes=...) override, unlike the sibling `expense` action at line 119 which explicitly sets permission_classes=[IsAuthenticated]

apps/reports/api/views.py:57-58 uses request.user directly (would be AnonymousUser for an unauthenticated caller) and only conditionally checks division scope 'if division_id:' -- an anonymous request omitting `division` skips even that check

apps/reports/models.py:49 created_by is a nullable ForeignKey(AUTH_USER_MODEL, null=True), so serializer.save(created_by=AnonymousUser()) at line 74 will raise a Django FK type error (uncaught) rather than silently succeeding -- currently fails closed by accident (unhandled 500), not by design

recommendation.fix_example: Add permission_classes = [permissions.IsAuthenticated] at ReportViewSet class level (as the `expense` action already does per-action), so list/retrieve/generate/status/download are consistently gated rather than depending on incidental get_queryset() checks or an FK-type crash.

findings.title: GET /api/statuses/planned/ schema declares single EmployeeStatusSerializer but response is a {current, planned} wrapper object
GET /api/statuses/{id}/history/ schema declares responses={200: EmployeeStatusSerializer} (single object) but handler returns a many=True list
GET /api/notifications/unread/ has no @extend_schema at all for a many=True list action
GET /api/secondments/incoming/ and /api/secondments/outgoing/ never call paginate_queryset — response is an unbounded, unpaginated list, and also has no @extend_schema

POST /api/employees/{id}/transfer/ takes division_id/position_id directly from request.data with no serializer validation — non-numeric division_id raises unhandled ValueError (int(division_id)); non-existent division_id/position_id reaches employee.save() and can raise a raw IntegrityError instead of a clean 400

POST /api/employees/{id}/transfer/ writes EmployeeTransferHistory (and would apply staffing counters) BEFORE the DIRECTORATE_HEAD/DIVISION_HEAD scope check; the scope check's 403 Response is returned from inside the same transaction.atomic() block, which commits normally on a plain return (no exception raised) — so a rejected/forbidden transfer still permanently persists a history row describing a transfer that never actually happened (employee.division was never reassigned, since employee.save() at line 163 is after the 403 return)

POST /api/employees/{id}/dismiss/ assigns request.data.get('dismissal_date') straight to a model DateField with no serializer/format validation; a malformed value is not caught before employee.save() and can surface as a raw DB error instead of a 400

POST /api/divisions/{id}/move/ calls int(parent_id) on raw request.data with no prior type check — a non-numeric parent_id (e.g. a string) raises an unhandled ValueError and surfaces as a 500 instead of a 400

EmployeeViewSet.perform_create wraps the initial EmployeeStatus.objects.create() call in a bare `except Exception: pass`, silently discarding any error (validation failure, IntegrityError, etc.) during initial status assignment on employee creation with no logging or client-visible signal
CI workflow runs only makemigrations --check; the 3107-test pytest suite and ruff lint never execute in CI
findings.notes: The only job is migrations-check (makemigrations --check --dry-run). No step runs `pytest`, `ruff check`, or any frontend gate. A regression that breaks the documented 3107/3107 gate (Status.md 21.08.2026) can merge to main without CI ever noticing — the gate is entirely developer-discipline-enforced. Recommendation: add a `test` job running `PR_TEST_DB_NAME=ci ./.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` and a `lint` job running `ruff check .`, both against the same Postgres service container pattern already used for the migrations-check DB. Regression test: push a commit that fails an existing test and confirm CI goes red.

findings.title: Django Admin registers business/operational models (Employee, EmployeeStatus, StatusChangeHistory, StatusDocument, Vacancy, StaffUnit, SecondmentRequest, Division, OpsSubmissionControlSettings, OpsDivisionNotifyRecipient), not just catalogs/dictionaries — bypassing the service layer that enforces the one-active-status invariant
findings.notes: django.contrib.admin is enabled (config/settings/base.py) and mounted at /admin/ (config/urls.py:10) — this is a reachable surface, not dead code, but requires is_staff (already-privileged actor), which caps severity at `low` per the severity rubric. ModelAdmin.save_model() calls full_clean() via ModelForm but does NOT route through the domain service (apps/statuses create_status()) that enforces 'one active status per employee' (see EmployeeStatus.save(), organization_management/apps/statuses/models.py:250-266 — full_clean() only checks pairwise overlap via clean(), the create_status() service-level default-closure logic in the service layer is bypassed entirely when creating/editing via /admin/). A staff user could create two ACTIVE overlapping statuses through Admin that the normal API path prevents. Vault records this exact architectural rule ('Admin = только справочники') as a *tested guard* in the archived Backend/VAPS stack (obsidian-vault/Personnel-Records/Decisions.md:474-479, tests test_admin_registry_is_exactly_catalogs / test_operations_does_not_import_core_models) but grep confirms neither test exists anywhere in the current Personnel-Records tests/ tree — the guard was never re-created after the port, so this is a live, currently-unenforced regression risk, not just a style nit. Recommendation: either (a) restrict admin.py registrations to genuine reference/dictionary models (Position, Rank, Role, Permission are legitimate; Employee/EmployeeStatus/StaffUnit/Division/SecondmentRequest are not) by removing @admin.register for business models and exposing them read-only if audit access is needed, or (b) port test_admin_registry_is_exactly_catalogs as a regression guard. Regression test: assert `admin.site._registry` keys are a fixed allowlist of catalog models.

findings.title: No ruff/mypy configuration found at Personnel-Records root — type/contract-safety row of the testing matrix is not_applicable because there is no gate to run
findings.notes: Auto-memory records 'ruff format scoping' and 'DB-уровень для инвариантов' feedback implying ruff IS used in this project's workflow, but no pyproject.toml/ruff.toml/setup.cfg with a [tool.ruff] or [tool.mypy] section was found at the Personnel-Records root during this pass — could not verify current config location within this audit's time budget. Reported as info/not fully investigated rather than asserted as a defect; needs a follow-up targeted grep for ruff config across the whole repo before treating as confirmed.

findings.title: Legacy statuses app derives "today" from timezone.now().date() (UTC), not local Asia/Almaty date — status state and day-boundary checks drift by one calendar day during ~00:00-05:00 local time

fix_example.note: Replace every `timezone.now().date()` (and `date.today()` in views.py:575) in organization_management/apps/statuses/{models.py,application/services.py,api/views.py,tasks.py,signals.py} and reports/infrastructure/data_aggregator.py:115 with `timezone.localdate()` (Django's local-timezone-aware helper), or route through the operations app's existing organization_management.apps.operations.clock.Clock.today_local() for consistency with the already-correct sibling app.

findings.notes: organization_management/config/settings/base.py:116 sets TIME_ZONE = 'Asia/Almaty' (UTC+5) with USE_TZ = True (line 118), confirmed by grep. Under USE_TZ=True, django.utils.timezone.now() returns an aware UTC datetime; calling .date() on it truncates in UTC, not in the local zone. Asia/Almaty is UTC+5, so local 00:00-04:59 corresponds to UTC 19:00-23:59 of the PREVIOUS calendar day — for that ~5-hour nightly window, `timezone.now().date()` returns yesterday's date while the true local business date is already today. This is exactly the bug class the sibling `operations` app was built to avoid: its own Clock module (clock.py, read in full) explicitly documents this hazard and provides Clock.today_local() precisely to sidestep it, and a codebase-wide grep confirms the operations app has ZERO raw timezone.now().date()/date.today() usages outside tests. The legacy `apps/statuses` app (still live: registered in INSTALLED_APPS, wired at /api/statuses/ in config/urls.py, and is the backing service for the EmployeeStatusViewSet used by the frontend's status-update dialogs) never adopted this discipline — 15 raw occurrences across models.py, application/services.py, api/views.py, tasks.py, signals.py. The most consequential is EmployeeStatus.save() (models.py:253), which is the SOLE deriver of lifecycle state (PLANNED/ACTIVE/COMPLETED) on every save — during the nightly UTC-lag window a status whose start_date is the true local today will still compare `self.start_date > today` as True (today read as yesterday) and be misclassified PLANNED instead of ACTIVE, or a status whose end_date was actually local-yesterday will still read as not-yet-ended and stay ACTIVE. This state feeds headcount/absence reporting (get_division_headcount, get_absence_statistics) and the two daily Celery tasks (apply_planned_statuses_task, complete_expired_statuses via services.py) whose entire job is to act at day boundaries — if either is scheduled near local midnight (typical for a 'daily rollover' job) the UTC-lag window is exactly when they'd run and could roll the WRONG day. I did not execute the code or a test run (no execution budget this pass, static audit only) so I could not directly observe the misclassification in a live process; the reasoning is a direct trace of Django's documented timezone.now() semantics against the confirmed settings and the read code, capping confidence at 0.6 per the calibration rule for an unverified-by-execution finding.

findings.title: Status-edit dialog discards the backend's specific validation/conflict message and shows a fixed generic string, hiding why an edit was rejected

related.symbol: fetchStatuses catch block (raw HTTP-error text surfaced instead)

fix_example.note: In the catch block at PlannedStatusesDialog.tsx:238-240, use lib/api.ts's own `extractApiErrorMessage` (already used by createEmployeeStatus at line 1152) against `e instanceof Error ? e.message : ''` before falling back to the generic string, mirroring the pattern already applied in the fetchStatuses catch a few lines above it.

findings.notes: Traced the full path by reading code, not by executing it (static audit, capped confidence). ApiClient.updateEmployeeStatusById (lib/api.ts:1050-1097) PATCHes the legacy `/api/statuses/statuses/{id}/` endpoint; on a non-2xx response it reads the response body as text and throws `new Error("HTTP error! status: ${status} - ${errorText}")` (lib/api.ts:1086-1088) — the errorText DOES contain the backend's structured reason, since EmployeeStatusViewSet.create's ValidationError handler (api/views.py:120-131, itself carefully written to avoid dumping a Python dict repr to the user) formats failures as {'error': '<human message>', 'errors': [...]}. But the caller in PlannedStatusesDialog.tsx's handleSaveEdit (line 218-243) catches this Error at line 238 and, instead of reading `e.message` (as the sibling fetchStatuses handler at line 177-182 does, or as createEmployeeStatus's caller elsewhere does via extractApiErrorMessage), discards it entirely and calls `setError("Не удалось обновить статус")` — a fixed generic string with zero information about which field or business rule failed (e.g. a hard/soft status-overlap conflict, a past-date rejection, or a permission gate). This specifically breaks visibility into the override workflow: the operations app's status_service.py (read in full) is built around returning a distinguishable 409 STATUS_OVERLAP_WARNING (soft, overridable) vs 422 OVERLAPPING_HARD_STATUS (hard, not overridable) with conflict details — losing that distinction at the UI boundary means an operator whose edit hit a soft, overridable conflict cannot tell that from a hard block, or from any other rejection reason. Severity is medium (non-golden-path usability degradation, not a broken golden path) since the user can still retry or investigate via other screens; scope is limited to this one dialog's edit-save handler, not the create-status path (which already extracts the message correctly), and not a data-loss or security issue.

findings.title: personnelFields() normalizer accepts `emp: any` with no compile-time contract, despite being the single shared mapper for three screens
findings.notes: The function's own docstring explains it exists BECAUSE the same personal-fields shape used to be assembled independently in three places (/employees, cards, /statuses) with inconsistent blank-field fallbacks — i.e. it is explicitly the seam meant to keep those three call sites in sync. Typing its input `emp: any` (from-api.ts:28) means that seam has no compile-time check: a raw API payload missing `current_status`, `rank`, `iin_masked`, etc., or a backend field rename (e.g. `last_name`/`first_name` at line 32, accessed with no null-guard, unlike the `??` fallbacks used for every other field below it), would only surface as a runtime `undefined`/exception rather than a type error at the call site. I did not find an observed instance of actual drift (no failing test, no reproduced runtime error) — this is a contract-safety gap on a boundary function, not a confirmed live bug, so severity is capped low and status is `proposed` rather than `confirmed`.

findings.title: entities/employee imports from features/, reversing FSD dependency direction

related.note: only consumer of EmployeeTable; transitively pulls features/employee-status-update into an entity-layer component tree

fix_example.text: Move the status-edit trigger out of EmployeeTable (entities layer) into a widget or the features/employee-status-update slice itself, e.g. render EditStatusDialog from app/employees/page.tsx (or a widgets/employee-list wrapper) and pass an onEditStatus callback prop into EmployeeTable instead of importing the dialog directly.

findings.notes: import EditStatusDialog from '@/features/employee-status-update/ui/EditStatusDialog' at entities/employee/ui/EmployeeTable.tsx:35. FSD convention (and this project's own app/ -> widgets/ -> features/ -> entities/ -> shared/ layering) requires entities to be feature-agnostic; here the entity component directly imports a feature. Static/structural finding only — no runtime break observed or claimed; impact is coupling/maintainability debt (entities/employee can no longer be reused or tested without the features slice), hence severity low rather than medium.

findings.title: Django Admin registers business/workflow records (EmployeeStatus, SecondmentRequest) with unrestricted add/delete, giving a second mutation path around the governing services and around the request-scoped audit middleware

related.note: no has_delete_permission override -> EmployeeStatus, the record protected by the 'exactly one active status per employee' invariant (obsidian-vault Personnel-Records/Decisions.md #Один-активный-статус-на-сотрудника), can be deleted directly from Admin

the governing service path this Admin registration bypasses: approve() creates a scoped EmployeeStatus, checks for existing ACTIVE conflicts, enforces division-of-decision-maker scoping (line ~76) before mutating .status
AuditMiddleware only fires for request.path.startswith('/api/'); Django Admin requests never go through it, so any mutation made via these two admin registrations is entirely unaudited

fix_example.text: Follow the pattern already established in operations/admin.py and operations/tests/test_admin_registry.py: either drop admin.site.register(SecondmentRequest) entirely (workflow is API-driven via approve/reject/cancel), or register it read-only (has_add_permission/has_change_permission/has_delete_permission all False, list/detail view only). For EmployeeStatus, add has_delete_permission returning False (mirroring StatusChangeHistoryAdmin's own delete-lock) so the invariant 'every working employee has an active status' cannot be silently broken outside StatusApplicationService, and cannot happen without an audit trail.

findings.notes: SecondmentRequest.status is a workflow field ('pending'/'approved'/'rejected'/'cancelled') mutated with business rules only inside SecondmentRequestViewSet.approve/reject/cancel (division-scope check, conflict check against existing ACTIVE EmployeeStatus, creation of the paired status record). admin.site.register(SecondmentRequest) with zero ModelAdmin customization exposes the same 'status' field for direct edit with none of those checks. For EmployeeStatus: creation via Admin DOES run full_clean() (Django ModelForm validation), so the overlap/single-active-status invariant is still enforced on create/change; StatusChangeHistory logging for create/change is also still triggered via the statuses/signals.py post_save receiver regardless of entry point. However deletion is NOT covered by any signal (log_status_change is post_save only) and is NOT blocked by the ModelAdmin (has_delete_permission not overridden), so an admin user can delete an EmployeeStatus row with zero history/audit trace and no compensating mechanism to restore the invariant. Confidence capped at 0.55: this is a static permission-surface read, not a reproduced deletion via an actual superuser session.

findings.title: PLANNED-to-ACTIVE status transition depends solely on a Celery task that does not run on the local stand, with no read-time reconciliation (unlike the parallel EXPIRED-status path, which does have one)

related.note: active_status()/status_on_date() both filter state=ACTIVE only; neither reconciles a PLANNED status whose start_date has already passed. Compare to the documented, deliberate handling of the EXPIRED-status case (module docstring lines 1-28): a status past end_date stays visible as 'ACTIVE but overdue' specifically so it isn't silently hidden; no equivalent exists for PLANNED status becoming due.

CELERY_BROKER_URL = 'redis://redis:6379/0' — docker-only hostname, unreachable on the local (non-docker) stand per obsidian-vault Personnel-Records/Known-Issues.md '# Celery-задачи статусов не доезжают на стенде'

fix_example.text: Give status_on_date()/active_status() (or a new selector) the same treatment already applied to the expired-status case: when the current DB-recorded active status is None or COMPLETED but a PLANNED status's start_date <= today exists, surface it at read time (flagged, as the expired case already flags overdue rows) instead of returning 'no status'. Alternatively/additionally, call StatusApplicationService.apply_planned_statuses() opportunistically from a request-scoped or scheduled synchronous path when Celery is known to be unreachable in the given environment.

findings.notes: Known-Issues.md documents this invariant break has already manifested on the local stand (7 of 14 working employees ended up without an active status after the 19.08.2026 smoke sweep) and names apply_planned_statuses/complete_expired_statuses as the two Celery-only closers, with ensure_employee_statuses as the manual workaround. The selectors.py docstring shows the EXPIRED path was deliberately given read-time visibility precisely because the closer might not have run yet ('Статус с истёкшим end_date остаётся ACTIVE в базе, пока его не закроет complete_expired_statuses_task, и это состояние надо ПОКАЗЫВАТЬ'). No equivalent statement or code exists for the PLANNED path: status_on_date() and active_status() both hard-filter state=ACTIVE, so a due-but-unapplied PLANNED status is invisible to every read path until the Celery task (or the manual ensure_employee_statuses command) runs — this is the absent-and-relied-upon case, reported as a finding per the task instructions. Confidence 0.55: reasoned from selector code + already-documented stand incident, not independently reproduced in this run.

findings.title: AuditMiddleware's id-extraction-from-JSON-response contract silently drops audit logging for the operations bulk status-create endpoint (and any other action returning a list/summary body without a top-level 'id')

fix_example.text: AuditMiddleware is the project's only mutation-audit mechanism and it is entirely response-shape-driven (target_object_id = response_data.get('id'), guarded by 'if content_type and target_object_id' at middleware.py:117). Any action that legitimately returns a summary/count instead of a single object with 'id' (this bulk endpoint returns {'created': N}) is invisibly excluded — no error, no log, nothing to grep for. Either (a) have bulk_create_statuses write one AuditLog row per created EmployeeStatus explicitly in operations/services layer (service-level, not middleware), or (b) extend AuditMiddleware to also handle a documented 'ids': [...] response convention for bulk endpoints, and audit every id in the list.

findings.notes: The project has no per-viewset/service audit decorator — AuditMiddleware (organization_management/apps/audit/middleware.py) is the sole coverage mechanism, and it works purely off HTTP method + URL shape + a top-level 'id' key in the JSON response body. The operations bulk status-create action (SubmissionStatusViewSet or equivalent, operations/api/views.py:1107-1127) creates N EmployeeStatus rows via bulk_create_statuses() and returns Response({'created': len(created)}, status=201) — no 'id' key, so target_object_id stays None and the AuditLog.objects.create call at middleware.py:118 never executes for this request, despite it being a genuine mutating, permission-gated (status.manage), conflict-checked bulk write. This is a real bypass of the stated audit-coverage mechanism, not a hypothetical one, distinct from Finding RAW-00000002-0 (Admin-path bypass) though both root-cause to the same gap: nothing in the codebase enforces 'every mutating write gets an audit row' as an invariant that fails loudly when unmet.

findings.title: GVO registry "Mine" filter links events to the current user by exact FIO string match (`ownerName === user.name`) — the documented forbidden pattern is live, not merely absent

related.note: same ownerName field also used to derive the 'responsible' person block by string equality against empty string, not identity

fix_example.text: obsidian-vault/Frontend/Status.md (2026-08-23 entry, 'Приведение к прототипу') explicitly states this exact pattern is a forbidden project rule and cites it as the reason the events registry's own 'Мои/Все' tabs were NOT built: '«свой» ОМ определяется только сопоставлением ФИО с ownerName, а склейка по имени в проекте запрещена'. That principle was honored in app/security-ops/events/page.tsx (no scope=mine filter exists there), but the GVO registry page (app/security-ops/gvo/page.tsx:66-73) independently implements the exact same forbidden pattern for its own 'Мои'/'Все' toggle, with an in-code comment acknowledging the tradeoff ('Без host-логина... владельца определить нечем'). Two employees sharing a display name would misclassify each other's events as 'Мои'; a legitimate owner whose display name diverges from event.ownerName (e.g. after a name change, or if ownerName falls back to username/id per Personnel-Records/Known-Issues.md) would see their own events missing from 'Мои'. Recommend either removing the scope=mine toggle from the GVO registry (matching the events registry's documented abstention) or routing 'mine' determination through a stable identifier once the backend exposes one, consistent with the project-wide ban on name-string linkage.

findings.title: Four files hand-roll a local `formatMoment(iso)` timestamp formatter instead of using the project's canonical `formatIsoDateTime` helper that the Aug-2026 date-formatting rollout introduced

related.note: canonical formatIsoDateTime helper these four duplicates reimplement

fix_example.text: Each of the four `formatMoment(iso)` functions is byte-identical (manual `getDate`/`getMonth`/`getHours` padding to DD.MM.YYYY, HH:MM) and produces output functionally equivalent to shared/lib/date.ts's `formatIsoDateTime`, which was built specifically to centralize this logic per obsidian-vault/Frontend/Known-Issues.md's date-handling entries. Not currently a visible defect (both paths render correct local-time strings), but it is exactly the kind of manual, un-consolidated step the business-process checklist flags: any future correction to timestamp formatting (locale options, fallback text, DST edge cases) applied to the shared helper will silently miss these four call sites. Replace all four local formatMoment definitions with imports of formatIsoDateTime.

findings.title:
User-submitted free text (comment body, feedback description/steps/contact) renders in plain `

` tags with zero break-words/overflow-wrap handling anywhere in the security-ops feature/app tree

related.note: request.description / expectedResult / reproductionSteps / contact — all free text, same pattern

fix_example.text:
`grep -rc "break-words\|break-all\|overflow-wrap" app/security-ops features --include="*.tsx"` returns zero hits across all 74 files. Default CSS `overflow-wrap: normal` on the affected `

` elements (inside `rounded-lg border p-2` list items and a `rounded-xl border` card, both without an explicit `overflow-x` guard) means a single long unbroken token pasted into a free-text field — a URL, a long filename, an accidentally pasted base64/UUID string in the 'contact' or 'description' fields of the incoming feedback form — will overflow its container and can push the surrounding layout wider than the viewport, since these are user-submitted strings with no length cap enforced client-side. Add `break-words` (Tailwind's `overflow-wrap: break-word`) to the free-text `

` elements in the feedback detail view (and any other screen rendering unbounded user text, e.g. security-event comments).
